text:
**Review Result**

Overall quality: **6/10**. The code is readable, compact, and has a decent test suite, but I would not approve it as-is because the core ingestion/upsert path can corrupt historical job state and resource accounting in realistic re-ingest scenarios.

Tests: `61 passed`; only warning was pytest being unable to write cache under read-only `/work`.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change scope: **~320 lines** including production fixes, migrations/indexing, and regression tests.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this PR as-is.**

**Findings**

- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:70): High: Same-rank updates can regress newer RUNNING/SUSPENDED snapshots when an older dump is re-ingested.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:31): High: Unknown Slurm states are treated as terminal, so real transitional states can block later valid progress.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:74): High: “Unchanged” detection ignores user, partition, submit/start, CPU/GPU allocation, and exit code changes.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:149): Medium: Negative CPU/GPU allocations are accepted and can produce negative usage totals.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:152): Medium: Empty user, partition, and exit-code fields are accepted instead of rejected or normalized.
- [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:14): Medium: Timestamp filtering uses lexicographic TEXT comparisons, which breaks for timezone-aware ISO values.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13): Medium: Schema has no indexes for report filters/grouping, so reports will full-scan as the database grows.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13): Medium: There is no schema versioning or migration path for future active development.
- [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:121): Low: Report commands create a new empty database on typo/missing `--db` paths instead of failing clearly.
- [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:7): Low: Package version is duplicated in `pyproject.toml` and `jobwatch/__init__.py`, creating drift risk.

issues.description: Same-rank updates can regress newer RUNNING/SUSPENDED snapshots when an older dump is re-ingested.
Unknown Slurm states are treated as terminal, so transitional states can block later valid progress.
Unchanged detection ignores corrected user, partition, submit/start, CPU/GPU allocation, and exit code fields.
Negative CPU/GPU allocations are accepted and can produce negative usage totals.
Empty user, partition, and exit-code fields are accepted instead of rejected or normalized.
Timestamp filtering uses lexicographic TEXT comparisons, which breaks for timezone-aware ISO values.
Schema has no indexes for report filters/grouping, causing full scans as the database grows.
Database schema has no versioning or migration mechanism for future changes.
Report commands create a new empty database on typo/missing --db paths instead of failing clearly.
Package version is duplicated in two files, creating drift risk.
